stanzas: Olav på det land har malet
Kvinner selv stod op og strede,
det gav døden selv sin ære —
vi med undren mot ham hastet;
Drevne frem på stand av skammen
nu vi står tre brødre sammen,
Norske mann i hus og hytte,
Og som fædres kamp har hævet
også vi, når det blir krævet,
orig.credit: Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson (1859–1868), in his original spelling

stanzas: Olav upon that land has painted
Tordenskjold flashed like lightning along the coast,
so that it was lighted home.
Women themselves stood up and fought,
when we were tested a few times,
for we would rather burn the land
than let it come to its fall;
but in the worst need, blue-eyed
That gave a father's strength to bear
it gave death itself its honour —
The enemy threw down his weapon,
we hastened towards him in wonder;
Driven up onto our feet [?] by the shame,
now we stand three brothers together,
The land he willed to protect,
All that the fathers have fought for,
the Lord has quietly set right,
so that we won our right.
And as the fathers' struggle has raised
we too, when it is demanded,
will pitch camp for its peace.

notes: line 1.2: 'som det stiger frem' is 'as it rises up, comes into view' (seen from the sea).
lines 1.7-1.8: 'saganat' is 'saga-night', the night of the old sagas, which 'sænker' (lets sink, lowers) dreams on the land.
line 2.1: 'bærget' (modern 'berget') can mean 'saved, secured' or 'gathered in' (as a harvest); here Harald gathering the land under his rule.
line 2.2: 'kjæmperad' is a row or rank of warriors, champions.
line 2.4: 'kvad' is 'chanted, sang (a poem)', as a skald; Øjvind is the skald Eyvind (Old Norse Eyvindr).
lines 2.7-2.8: 'talet Roma midt imod' is 'spoke out right against Rome', i.e. defied Rome.
line 3.4: 'så den lystes hjæm' is literally 'so that it was lighted home'; 'den' can be the army of line 3.2 (lit on its way home, sent back) or the coast; the sense is disputed.
line 3.8: 'men det kom igjæn' is 'but it came again': what came back is not named; it is usually taken as the land's fortune or freedom.
line 4.2: 'strak dog til' is 'were still enough, sufficed'.
line 4.8: Fredrikshald is the town now called Halden.
line 6.2: 'op visiret fór' is 'up went the visor' (of a helmet).
line 6.5: 'Drevne frem på stand av skammen' is hard to render: literally 'driven forth on stand by the shame'; read as 'roused to stand up (to take a stand) by the shame'.
line 7.7: 'læmpet' is 'eased, adjusted, gently set in order'.
line 8.8: 'slår lejr' is 'pitches camp, encamps': the people will take the field for the land's peace.
